settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit optimization with reward function in an RKHS (agnostic setting)
unmapped: Unknown f has RKHS norm ||f||_k <= B, B known to the learner (recorded via learner_knows S)
Regularisation lambda = 1 + 2/T depends on the horizon T
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of sequentially maximizing a fixed but unknown reward function $f:D\ra \Real$ over a (potentially infinite) set of decisions $D \subset \Real^d$ ... We assume that the noise sequence ... is conditionally $R$-sub-Gaussian ... we assume that $D$ is compact ... We assume a known bound on the RKHS norm of the unknown target function: $\norm{f}_k \le B$. Moreover, we assume bounded variance by restricting $k(x,x) \le 1$

unmapped: Kernel k known with k(x,x) <= 1; discretization uses kernel smoothness constant L and box size r
D compact and convex, contained in [0,r]^d
settings.definition_quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $D \subset [0,r]^d$ be compact and convex, $\norm{f}_k \le B$ and $\{\epsilon_t\}_t$ a conditionally $R$-sub-Gaussian sequence.

symbols.B_norm: known upper bound on the RKHS norm ||f||_k of the reward function

conditions: k(x,x) <= 1 for all x in D

source.label: thm:regret-bound-UCB
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $\norm{f}_k \le B$ and $\epsilon_t$ is conditionally $R$-sub-Gaussian. Running IGP-UCB for a function $f$ lying in the RKHS $H_k(D)$, we obtain a regret bound of $O\Big(\sqrt{T}(B\sqrt{\gamma_T}+\gamma_T)\Big)$ with high probability. More precisely, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $R_T = O\Big(B\sqrt{T\gamma_T}+\sqrt{T\gamma_T(\gamma_T+\ln(1/\delta))}\Big)$.

results.notes: Noise level R treated as constant inside O. Horizon marked known because lambda = 1+2/T in the analysis. gamma_T is maximum information gain.

source.label: thm:regret-bound-TS
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $D \subset [0,r]^d$ be compact and convex, $\norm{f}_k \le B$ and $\{\epsilon_t\}_t$ a conditionally $R$-sub-Gaussian sequence. Running GP-TS for a function $f$ lying in the RKHS $H_k(D)$ and with decision sets $D_t$ chosen as above, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of GP-TS satisfies $R_T=O\Big(\sqrt{(\gamma_T+\ln(2/\delta))d\ln (BdT)} \Big(\sqrt{T\gamma_T}+B\sqrt{T\ln(2/\delta)}\Big)\Big)$.

results.notes: Constants L, r, R absorbed. Paper summarizes as Õ(γ_T sqrt(dT)). Discretization is exponential in d.
